newsitem.title: USA: NYC MAC weighs $2 billion refunding in one year.
newsitem.headline: NYC MAC weighs $2 billion refunding in one year.

text.p: The Municipal Assistance Control Board of New York City on Monday said it was considering refunding as much as $2 billion of callable bonds within the year.
"We're headed to about a $2 billion refunding in the future," said Edward Regan, the chairman of the MAC, at the board's annual meeting.
The control board in April issued approximately $917 million of refunding bonds, a move it estimated saved $125 million in interest costs in 1996 and about $1.7 million each year until 2008.
MAC officials later said that the new refunding that was contemplated likely would occur within one year. They declined to disclose further details.
